Risk: The offline model on the corporate GPU platform judges less accurately than the cloud models the prototype was measured with.
Effect if it happens: Results are not trusted, or the AI governance approval is refused.
Mitigation: Benchmark the available models in month 1 to 2 on the evaluation cases. Agree the minimum acceptable accuracy before building further.

Risk: Reviewers cannot keep up. A human decides every result, and 2,000 applications with several hundred controls each is a very large yearly review load.
Effect if it happens: Backlog of unreviewed results. The speed benefit disappears.
Mitigation: Estimate reviewer effort from the pilot. Decide on control inheritance and on which results need full review.

Risk: A team of about five people with the right skills cannot be found from internal staff. The sponsor has already said resource is short.
Effect if it happens: Later start, slower delivery, or a team without the skills to pass authorisation.
Mitigation: Name the team before approval. Where a role cannot be filled, decide between delaying, contracting or reducing scope.

Risk: The MVP is not authorised at the HIGH baseline within 12 months, because the assessment and approval steps are paced by other teams.
Effect if it happens: Go-live slips. Team cost continues at roughly £40k to £65k a month while waiting.
Mitigation: Start authorisation work in month 1. Agree the assessment timetable and evidence format with the assessors up front. Review progress monthly with the authorising official.

Risk: Reviewers approve AI results without real scrutiny, especially at volume.
Effect if it happens: Human review becomes a formality and errors pass through.
Mitigation: Design the review screen so citations must be opened. Monitor override rates and time spent per review. Audit a sample of approvals.

Risk: The evaluation set does not represent real evidence. The prototype's set covers 13 controls with AI-written documents and AI-assigned labels.
Effect if it happens: Measured accuracy overstates real accuracy.
Mitigation: Build the set from realistic documents across all control families, labelled by named experts.

Risk: Accuracy on real evidence cannot be measured before go-live, because real evidence is only allowed in production and production cannot hold real data before authorisation.
Effect if it happens: The first real measure of quality comes after launch.
Mitigation: Agree an approach with the security team early: sanitised real documents, or a limited approval to test.

Risk: Business units do not take on the work of onboarding their applications and uploading evidence, although the ROM assumes they will.
Effect if it happens: Slow take-up. Few applications assessed.
Mitigation: Agree the onboarding commitment with each business unit head. Provide an onboarding guide and support.

Risk: The time saved by the AI is lost to human review, so elapsed assessment time does not fall.
Effect if it happens: The main benefit is not delivered.
Mitigation: Measure end-to-end time in the pilot, not just AI scoring time. Tune the review process on that evidence.

Risk: The build costs more than the point estimate because the hours are estimates anchored on a prototype built by one person, not on a team's measured delivery rate.
Effect if it happens: Cost rises towards the top of the ROM range (75% above the point estimate).
Mitigation: Have the delivery team review every Build line before approval. Re-baseline the estimate at month 3 using actual progress. Release funding milestone by milestone.

Risk: The scarce skills (AI engineers with retrieval and evaluation experience, security engineers with HIGH baseline experience) are not available, and recruitment and upskilling are excluded.
Effect if it happens: The hardest lines (assessment engine, evaluation, authorisation) are staffed by people learning on the job.
Mitigation: Identify these people by name. Budget training or specialist support if they are not available.

Risk: Knowledge of why the prototype works sits with one person.
Effect if it happens: The new design repeats mistakes the prototype already solved, or loses its quality.
Mitigation: Secure the prototype developer's time for the design phase. Turn the prototype's decision records and measured results into a design brief for the new team.

Risk: The prototype's pace does not carry over to a team working on a new design, because of coordination, reviews and enterprise process.
Effect if it happens: Feature lines take up to twice the estimated hours.
Mitigation: Measure actual pace in the first two months and re-forecast. Keep the team small and co-located in working hours.

Risk: Business units do not release the customer subject matter experts for the 650 hours needed in Part 1.
Effect if it happens: No trusted evaluation set, so accuracy cannot be shown and the AI governance approval stalls.
Mitigation: Agree named experts and their time with their managers. Schedule labelling in blocks, not ad hoc.

Risk: Corporate lead times for virtual machines, storage, firewall rules, certificates and service accounts are longer than the first four months allow.
Effect if it happens: Development starts late or is done on unsuitable environments and reworked.
Mitigation: Raise all provisioning requests in the mobilisation month. Ask for a development environment first. Track each request as a dependency.

Risk: Scope grows towards a full governance, risk and compliance platform. This pattern was already seen while the ROM was being built.
Effect if it happens: Cost and duration rise with each addition.
Mitigation: Baseline the scope. Require any addition to displace an existing item or come with funding. Keep the Scope options tab as the parking place.

Risk: Control inheritance (assessing a shared control once for many applications) and per-application baseline selection turn out to be essential but are not in the costed scope.
Effect if it happens: Without inheritance, assessment and review volumes roughly double.
Mitigation: Decide in the opening design sprint. If needed, add it as a costed line before approval.

Risk: There is no agreed measure of what 'significantly speed up assessment' means.
Effect if it happens: The MVP is judged a failure against an unstated expectation.
Mitigation: Agree a measurable target and measure the current manual effort before the pilot starts.

Risk: Fewer controls can be inherited from corporate services than assumed.
Effect if it happens: More controls to implement and document than the 1,400 hours allow.
Mitigation: Do the inheritance analysis in months 1 to 2 with the security team, and re-estimate M16 from the result.

Risk: Sensitive evidence text sent to the model is copied into application logs, SIEM, monitoring tools or the GPU platform's own logs.
Effect if it happens: Sensitive data spreads to systems outside this system's access and disposal controls.
Mitigation: Decide what is logged where. Keep full prompts only in the protected audit store. Agree log handling with the GPU platform owner.

Risk: A wrong 'Met' result is accepted by a reviewer and a real control gap goes undetected.
Effect if it happens: False assurance. This is the most damaging type of error for an assurance tool.
Mitigation: Measure the false 'Met' rate separately and set a limit. Use a conservative rubric. Sample-check approved results.

Risk: Hidden instructions inside an evidence document manipulate the result. Evidence is supplied by the party being assessed, who benefits from a good score.
Effect if it happens: Results can be steered by whoever writes the evidence.
Mitigation: Treat all evidence as untrusted input. Include manipulation attempts in the evaluation set and in security testing.

Risk: The GPU platform cannot process the volume. At the prototype's speed one full pass of 2,000 applications is about 9,250 hours of scoring.
Effect if it happens: Yearly reassessment of all applications is not achievable.
Mitigation: Run the throughput benchmark in month 1. Decide on inheritance, batching and priorities from the result.

Risk: An access control flaw lets a user see another application's evidence or weaknesses through search, the assistant, reports or export.
Effect if it happens: Serious confidentiality breach. The prototype had this flaw in its assistant.
Mitigation: Enforce access in the data layer so every route inherits it. Test every route for data separation.

Risk: The programme that provides the GPU platform is delayed, cancelled or gives priority to other users.
Effect if it happens: The system cannot run at all without it.
Mitigation: Get a written commitment on availability, capacity and priority. Identify a fallback.

Risk: Run cost is not funded by go-live, so the MVP goes live with no team to support or maintain it.
Effect if it happens: Service is unsupported, vulnerabilities go unpatched and the authorisation lapses.
Mitigation: Agree the run budget and name a service owner by month 6. Make confirmed run funding a go-live condition.

Risk: The AI coding assistants that made the prototype's pace possible are not allowed for developing a HIGH system on the corporate network, or only weaker offline ones are.
Effect if it happens: Development speed falls sharply. Feature lines could double.
Mitigation: Confirm the policy on AI coding tools before approval. If restricted, re-estimate the feature lines on that basis.
ROM reference: M5 to M13, L2 to L15

Risk: A service the system relies on (GPU platform, virtual machine platform, SIEM, backup) is not itself authorised at the HIGH baseline.
Effect if it happens: The system cannot be authorised until that service is.
Mitigation: Check the authorisation status of every inherited service before approval.

Risk: The combined record of control weaknesses for 2,000 applications makes the system a prime target for attackers.
Effect if it happens: A breach would hand an attacker a map of the organisation's weaknesses.
Mitigation: Treat the data at the highest sensitivity it contains. Minimise standing access. Monitor for bulk access and export.

Risk: The same evidence gives a different result when assessed again. The prototype measured noticeable run-to-run variation.
Effect if it happens: Results are hard to defend to an auditor or a system owner.
Mitigation: Fix model settings, store every request and response, pin model and prompt versions, and re-run borderline cases.

Risk: The GPU platform changes or retires the model without notice.
Effect if it happens: Results shift overnight and comparison with earlier assessments is lost.
Mitigation: Agree model pinning and a notice period with the platform owner. Re-run the evaluation before any model change goes live.

Risk: Corporate policy bars certain open-weight models on grounds of origin. The open-weight models the prototype measured (GLM and DeepSeek families) may not be acceptable.
Effect if it happens: Fewer model choices and possibly lower accuracy.
Mitigation: Get the approved model list and provenance rules before benchmarking.

Risk: System owners learn what wording scores well and write documents to satisfy the AI instead of improving controls.
Effect if it happens: Scores rise without real improvement.
Mitigation: Weight operational proof above policy statements. Sample-audit high scores. Rotate evaluation cases.

Risk: Evidence quality is poor or uneven across the 2,000 applications, so most results are 'insufficient evidence'.
Effect if it happens: The tool is seen as adding little, although it is reporting the true position.
Mitigation: Set expectations with the pilot. Provide guidance on what good evidence looks like. Report evidence gaps as a useful output.

Risk: External auditors or regulators do not accept AI-assisted assessments as assurance.
Effect if it happens: Manual assessment has to continue in parallel, removing the benefit.
Mitigation: Involve internal audit and the external auditor from the design stage. Show them the human decision record and evidence trail.

Risk: There is no baseline of the effort manual assessments take today.
Effect if it happens: Benefits cannot be demonstrated afterwards.
Mitigation: Measure a sample of current manual assessments before the pilot.

Risk: Assessors lose trust after early visible errors and return to manual methods.
Effect if it happens: The tool is abandoned in practice.
Mitigation: Start with a small, supported pilot. Be open about known limits. Fix reported errors quickly and visibly.

Risk: During the transition assessors do both the manual assessment and the tool-based one.
Effect if it happens: Workload rises before it falls. Resentment.
Mitigation: Agree a date after which the tool result is the accepted result for pilot applications.

Risk: The architecture works at pilot scale but not for 5,000 users and 2,000 applications.
Effect if it happens: The scale-up in Part 2 costs far more than the 300 hours allowed.
Mitigation: Set scale targets in the design. Run a load test at realistic volume before the MVP design is fixed.

Risk: Backups of the three stores are not taken at the same point in time.
Effect if it happens: A restore produces mismatched data and unreliable results.
Mitigation: Design and test a coordinated backup and restore. Prove it in the disaster recovery test.

Risk: Disposal at three years misses copies in backups, the search index, logs or exports.
Effect if it happens: Breach of the retention rule.
Mitigation: Map every place evidence is copied to. Test disposal end to end.

Risk: Backup copies that cannot be altered conflict with the rule that documents must not be kept beyond three years.
Effect if it happens: Either backups breach retention, or backup protection is weakened.
Mitigation: Agree backup retention periods with records management and security before the backup design is fixed.

Risk: Disposal at three years removes evidence behind a finding that is still open, or evidence under legal hold.
Effect if it happens: A finding can no longer be evidenced. Possible legal exposure.
Mitigation: Define exceptions to disposal (open findings, legal hold) with records management and legal.

Risk: The corporate records system cannot accept complete assessment packages, because of format, size or lack of an interface.
Effect if it happens: Long-term traceability fails and the three-year disposal cannot safely run.
Mitigation: Agree the package format and transfer method with the records team in Part 1, before Drop B.

Risk: The corporate operating system build does not support Qdrant, MinIO, the document parsing tools or containers.
Effect if it happens: Product change or exceptions needed, with delay.
Mitigation: Confirm the build and what is permitted on it in the mobilisation month.

Risk: Made-up test data in the lower environments hides defects that only appear with real evidence.
Effect if it happens: Defects are found in production during the pilot.
Mitigation: Make synthetic data as realistic as possible in format and size. Plan a controlled early-life period.

Risk: Source system connectors take much more than 100 hours each, because of missing interfaces or poor data quality.
Effect if it happens: Fewer connectors delivered, or Part 2 overruns.
Mitigation: Survey each source system before committing. Deliver the simplest connectors first.

Risk: Accountability is unclear when an AI-assisted assessment misses a gap that later contributes to an incident.
Effect if it happens: Reputational damage and dispute over who was responsible.
Mitigation: Set a clear policy: the named human reviewer owns the decision, recorded with their rationale.

Risk: Actual internal hourly rates differ from the placeholder rates used in the estimate.
Effect if it happens: Every cost figure moves in proportion to the rate difference.
Mitigation: Replace the 14 placeholder rates on the Inputs sheet with finance-approved rates before the ROM is presented for approval.

Risk: Servers, storage or software licences assumed to come from existing corporate capacity are charged to the project.
Effect if it happens: Up to about £0.67M of hardware and £0.4M a year of licences fall on the project (indicative figures on the Summary sheet).
Mitigation: Get written confirmation from the infrastructure and licensing owners of what is provided free and what is charged.

Risk: Funding is approved for Part 1 only and there is a gap before Part 2 is approved.
Effect if it happens: The team disperses, knowledge is lost and Part 2 costs more to restart. The MVP stays at pilot scale.
Mitigation: Seek approval in principle for both parts, with a decision point at month 9. Keep the core team in place across the boundary.

Risk: The 30% contingency is not enough, because the work most likely to overrun (authorisation, corporate integrations, model accuracy) is controlled by other teams.
Effect if it happens: Contingency is used up before the MVP is authorised.
Mitigation: Track contingency use monthly. Agree in advance who can release further reserve and on what evidence.

Risk: The case for building is challenged because commercial compliance tools add AI assessment features during the 24 months.
Effect if it happens: Programme is paused or cancelled part way through, with sunk cost.
Mitigation: Record why building is preferred (offline model, verified citations, HIGH baseline). Repeat a short market scan at months 6 and 12.

Risk: The GPU platform has an outage or slows down, and assessments stop. The 99% availability target depends on a platform the project does not control.
Effect if it happens: Service target missed for reasons outside the team's control.
Mitigation: Agree a service level with the platform owner. Queue work and tell users when the platform is unavailable.

Risk: A team member leaves or is reassigned. In a five-person team each person is a fifth of capacity and may be the only holder of a skill.
Effect if it happens: Weeks of delay and loss of knowledge.
Mitigation: Pair people on critical areas. Keep design and operational documentation current.

Risk: The run team is not recruited or trained before go-live.
Effect if it happens: The build team carries support, delaying Part 2.
Mitigation: Start run team onboarding at month 9, with shadowing before handover.

Risk: The security assessment raises more findings than the 300 hours allowed for fixing them.
Effect if it happens: Authorisation delayed and extra development cost.
Mitigation: Run an internal pre-assessment at month 8. Involve assessors in the design reviews so findings surface early.

Risk: The penetration test finds serious weaknesses late, in months 10 to 11.
Effect if it happens: Little time to fix before the go-live date.
Mitigation: Do threat modelling in month 2 and security testing from month 6. Ask the penetration test team for an early look at the design.

Risk: Integrations with corporate services (sign-on, SIEM, backup, records system, task tool) slip because those teams have other priorities.
Effect if it happens: Features wait on other teams. Authorisation evidence is incomplete.
Mitigation: Agree a named contact and a delivery date for each integration. Escalate through the sponsor when a date is missed.

Risk: Design decisions left open (there is no discovery phase) are made late and cause rework.
Effect if it happens: Rework on access control, retention and integration design.
Mitigation: Hold a two-week decision sprint at the start to close the open decisions on the Basis and Issues tabs.

Risk: Part 2 drops slip because fixing MVP defects and supporting the pilot absorb the team after go-live.
Effect if it happens: Drop A moves out and Part 2 takes longer than 12 months.
Mitigation: Fund the run team from go-live so the build team is not also the support team.

Risk: Stakeholders treat the 152-requirement business requirements document as the committed scope, although the ROM covers a narrower assessment tool.
Effect if it happens: Dispute at acceptance. Pressure to add at least the £166k of scope options.
Mitigation: Mark each requirement as in Part 1, in Part 2, optional, or met by another corporate tool, and have the sponsor sign it off.

Risk: People who have seen the feature-rich prototype (95 screens) expect the MVP to match it and see the MVP as a step backwards.
Effect if it happens: Loss of confidence at the first demonstration.
Mitigation: Publish a plain comparison of prototype features against MVP and later drops. Demonstrate early and often.

Risk: The business asks for assessment against other standards (for example ISO 27001, the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework or internal policy), when only NIST SP 800-53 is costed.
Effect if it happens: Each further standard needs its own control content, rubric and evaluation set.
Mitigation: Confirm the standards needed in the first two years. Design the catalogue so further standards can be added without rework.

Risk: Starting from a new design loses behaviour the prototype had already proven, so assessment quality goes backwards.
Effect if it happens: Lower accuracy than the prototype demonstrated, found late.
Mitigation: Treat the prototype as the working specification. Carry over its evaluation cases and the intent of its tests as acceptance criteria.

Risk: Qdrant, MinIO or other open-source components do not use encryption modules validated to FIPS 140-3, which the HIGH baseline expects.
Effect if it happens: Compensating design, product change or a formal risk acceptance.
Mitigation: Confirm each component's position early. Use validated platform-level encryption where a product lacks it.

Risk: The assessors require personnel screening for administrators and developers, although vetting is excluded from the ROM.
Effect if it happens: Vetting cost and weeks of delay for affected staff.
Mitigation: Raise this with the authorising official before approval and get a written position.

Risk: The authorising official is unwilling to accept the remaining risks of a new kind of system that uses AI.
Effect if it happens: Authorisation refused or heavily conditioned.
Mitigation: Brief the authorising official early and regularly. Agree what evidence of AI quality and oversight they need.

Risk: A malicious upload (malware, a file crafted to attack the parser, or an oversized archive) compromises the ingestion servers.
Effect if it happens: Compromise of servers that handle all evidence.
Mitigation: Scan every upload before processing. Run parsing in an isolated, restricted environment.

Risk: The GPU platform is shared with other users, and evidence remains in memory, caches or logs.
Effect if it happens: Exposure of evidence to other platform users or administrators.
Mitigation: Confirm the platform's isolation model. Record it in the authorisation package.

Risk: Data exported to reporting tools or files leaves the system's access control and three-year disposal.
Effect if it happens: Sensitive data in uncontrolled copies.
Mitigation: Restrict export by role. Log every export. Agree handling rules for the reporting tool.

Risk: A model or prompt change produces wrong results at scale before anyone notices.
Effect if it happens: Many assessments have to be withdrawn and repeated.
Mitigation: No change goes live without passing the evaluation. Keep the ability to identify and re-score every result made by a given version.

Risk: The sponsor moves on or organisational priorities change during the build.
Effect if it happens: Loss of funding, decisions or momentum.
Mitigation: Name a deputy sponsor. Tie the programme to a standing governance board, not to one person.

Risk: An administrator or other privileged insider reads or exports weakness data.
Effect if it happens: Same exposure as an external breach, harder to detect.
Mitigation: Use privileged access management, separation of duties and alerts on unusual access.

Risk: Compromised open-source packages, container images or model files are brought onto the offline network.
Effect if it happens: Malicious code inside a HIGH system.
Mitigation: Bring software in only through a controlled, scanned route. Verify sources and checksums. Keep a bill of materials.

Risk: The new team does not apply the lessons from the prototype's defects, such as treating an unreadable AI reply as a pass.
Effect if it happens: The same integrity defects reappear in production.
Mitigation: Write the lessons as design rules with tests: any unrecognised AI output is a failure, never a default.

Risk: Long controls exceed the model's input or output limits. Some controls have up to 38 objectives, and the prototype saw cut-off replies misread as failures.
Effect if it happens: Some controls cannot be assessed, or fail unpredictably.
Mitigation: Test the longest controls in the benchmark. Split large controls. Detect cut-off replies explicitly.

Risk: Confidence scores are not calibrated, yet are used to decide which results get most review attention.
Effect if it happens: Review effort goes to the wrong results.
Mitigation: Do not use confidence for prioritising until it is shown to be reliable on expert-labelled data.

Risk: Scanned documents, diagrams and spreadsheets are read incorrectly.
Effect if it happens: Evidence is missed or misquoted.
Mitigation: Benchmark the parsing tools on real document types. Show the original beside the extracted text.

Risk: Reassessments bunch up before audit or year-end deadlines.
Effect if it happens: Long queues at the times results are most needed.
Mitigation: Schedule assessments across the year. Give interactive work priority over batch work.

Risk: The embedding model has to change later, which forces every document to be re-indexed.
Effect if it happens: Days of processing and a full re-evaluation.
Mitigation: Choose the embedding model deliberately at the start. Design the index so a new one can be built alongside the old.

Risk: The model is systematically lenient or harsh for particular control families or evidence types.
Effect if it happens: Hidden bias in the overall compliance picture.
Mitigation: Report accuracy by control family and evidence type, not just overall.

Risk: Search misses relevant evidence in a large document set and the control is wrongly reported as lacking evidence.
Effect if it happens: False gaps and wasted effort by system owners.
Mitigation: Measure retrieval separately from judgement. Let reviewers point the tool at a document.

Risk: System owners dispute AI-proposed findings.
Effect if it happens: Escalations and delay in closing assessments.
Mitigation: Give system owners a clear way to respond with further evidence before a finding is confirmed.

Risk: The pilot uses the best-documented applications and gives an over-optimistic picture.
Effect if it happens: Problems appear only at full rollout.
Mitigation: Choose pilot applications to cover a spread of size, type and evidence quality.

Risk: Exported or copied results are circulated without the caveats, review status or evidence trail.
Effect if it happens: Unreviewed AI output is taken as an official position.
Mitigation: Stamp every export with review status and date. Restrict export of unreviewed results.

Risk: Evidence volume is much larger than the 25 TB placeholder.
Effect if it happens: More storage and longer processing.
Mitigation: Sample real evidence from pilot applications in month 1 to 2 and re-size.

Risk: The three data stores (database, search index, file store) drift out of step, leaving orphaned or missing data. The prototype had this problem.
Effect if it happens: Results cite evidence that no longer exists, or deleted evidence stays searchable.
Mitigation: Build reconciliation across all three stores from the start and run it on a schedule.

Risk: Code written quickly with AI assistance is hard to maintain. The prototype has very large code units.
Effect if it happens: Slower change and more defects over time.
Mitigation: Set coding standards, size limits and mandatory human review from day one.

Risk: The data protection impact assessment finds personal data in evidence (names in access lists, incident reports, HR-related records) that needs controls not costed.
Effect if it happens: Extra design work or restrictions on what evidence can be uploaded.
Mitigation: Start the assessment in month 1. Involve the data protection officer in the design.

Risk: Staff see the tool as monitoring system owners or as replacing assessors.
Effect if it happens: Resistance, low cooperation, possible need for staff consultation.
Mitigation: Explain the purpose early. Involve assessors in the design. Check consultation duties with HR.

Risk: Open-source licence terms create obligations (MinIO is under the AGPL), or a vendor changes its licence.
Effect if it happens: Legal exposure or a forced product change.
Mitigation: Have legal review the licences of all components. Keep products behind standard interfaces so they can be swapped.

Risk: Records management later rules that stored AI prompts and outputs are records that must be kept for seven years.
Effect if it happens: More storage and a change to disposal rules.
Mitigation: Get a ruling from records management before the retention design is fixed.

Risk: Corporate teams (security assessment, penetration testing, infrastructure, service desk) charge their time back to the project.
Effect if it happens: Unplanned cost that could reach several hundred hours.
Mitigation: Confirm the charging position with each team and record it as a dependency agreement.

Risk: There is no vendor support for Qdrant or MinIO on an offline network. The prototype's records note the free edition of MinIO is in maintenance mode.
Effect if it happens: Slow fixes for faults. Possible product replacement.
Mitigation: Decide on paid support or an alternative product before the design is fixed.

Risk: A warm or cold standby does not meet the contingency controls of the HIGH baseline or the recovery time the business expects.
Effect if it happens: More disaster recovery investment than planned.
Mitigation: Agree recovery time and recovery point targets with the business and the assessors early.

Risk: The run team is too small to keep up with fixes, vulnerabilities and requested changes.
Effect if it happens: Growing backlog and declining trust.
Mitigation: Review run team size after three months of live service.

Risk: Experts disagree with each other about the correct judgement, which limits how well the AI can be measured.
Effect if it happens: Accuracy targets are argued over. Extra adjudication effort.
Mitigation: Have two experts label each case, measure their agreement and resolve differences in a moderated session.

Risk: Corporate change freezes (year end, audit periods, major incidents) block deployments at critical points.
Effect if it happens: Milestones slip by weeks at a time.
Mitigation: Get the change calendar for the next 24 months and plan milestones around it.

Risk: The busiest period (months 3 to 6) needs more people than the team has.
Effect if it happens: Tasks slip into later months and compress testing.
Mitigation: Level the plan once the real team is known. Protect testing time when re-planning.

Risk: NIST publishes an update to the control catalogue during the build, changing control or objective identifiers.
Effect if it happens: Re-import, re-mapping and re-running the evaluation.
Mitigation: Store the catalogue version with every result. Build the import so a new version can sit alongside the old one.

Risk: The MVP scope the sponsor has in mind differs from the Part 1 list in this ROM.
Effect if it happens: Rework of the plan and estimate after approval.
Mitigation: Walk through the Part 1 MVP plan line by line with the sponsor and record agreement.

Risk: Operational technology assets are judged with rules written for IT systems.
Effect if it happens: Wrong results for those assets, for example penalising the absence of active scanning.
Mitigation: Carry over the prototype's separate rule set for operational technology and test it with specialists.

Risk: Patching is slow on an offline network.
Effect if it happens: Known vulnerabilities stay open beyond the allowed time.
Mitigation: Agree the patch route and timings with the infrastructure team. Fund it in the run team.

Risk: Each Part 2 drop is a significant change that needs security re-assessment, and the 300 hours allowed is too little.
Effect if it happens: Drops wait for security approval.
Mitigation: Agree with the assessors what counts as a significant change and plan re-assessment into each drop.

Risk: Ongoing security duties after go-live (monitoring, yearly reassessment, managing open actions) are under-resourced.
Effect if it happens: The authorisation lapses.
Mitigation: Include these duties in the run team's remit and budget.

Risk: A citation that does not really support the claim passes the automatic check, for example through a loose text match.
Effect if it happens: A result looks evidenced when it is not.
Mitigation: Use strict matching by default. Show the matched passage to the reviewer. Measure citation validity in the evaluation.

Risk: The stored record of control weaknesses has to be disclosed in litigation, a regulatory enquiry or an information request.
Effect if it happens: Sensitive weakness data becomes available to outside parties.
Mitigation: Take legal advice on how these records are classified and handled.

Risk: The organisation decides to buy an enterprise compliance or AI platform that overlaps with this tool.
Effect if it happens: Duplication or cancellation.
Mitigation: Keep enterprise architecture informed. Position the tool against the corporate roadmap.

Risk: AI technology moves on during the 24 months and design choices become dated.
Effect if it happens: Some rework to adopt better models or methods.
Mitigation: Keep the model and retrieval behind clean interfaces. Review the approach at each drop.

Risk: Pay and price inflation over the 24-month build is not in the estimate, which is at today's prices.
Effect if it happens: A few percent of extra cost in year two.
Mitigation: Apply the organisation's standard inflation assumption when the ROM is turned into a budget.

Risk: Existing capacity is not enough and new hardware has to be bought, with a procurement lead time.
Effect if it happens: Months of delay for production or disaster recovery environments.
Mitigation: Confirm capacity in the mobilisation month. If a purchase is needed, raise it immediately.

Risk: The internal assessment team is not considered independent enough of the delivery team (the HIGH baseline calls for independent assessors).
Effect if it happens: Assessment has to be repeated by another team.
Mitigation: Agree the assessors and their independence with the authorising official at the start.

Risk: The licence of the chosen model restricts enterprise use or changes later.
Effect if it happens: Forced model change and re-evaluation.
Mitigation: Have legal review the licence before the model is adopted. Record it in the model register.

Risk: The knowledge assistant gives confident advice that people act on outside the governed assessment process.
Effect if it happens: Decisions made on unreviewed AI output.
Mitigation: Label assistant answers clearly, show sources, and keep assessments as the only route to a recorded result.

Risk: AI regulation or internal AI policy tightens during the build.
Effect if it happens: New documentation, testing or oversight duties.
Mitigation: Align to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework from the start. Review policy changes quarterly.

Risk: The 300 hours allowed for training and rollout to 5,000 users is not enough.
Effect if it happens: Patchy use and avoidable support calls.
Mitigation: Use short role-based e-learning and a network of local champions.

Risk: Corporate tools the system integrates with (identity, task tool, SIEM, reporting) are upgraded or replaced.
Effect if it happens: Rework of integrations.
Mitigation: Use standard interfaces. Track the roadmaps of those tools.

Risk: Qdrant search slows down as the index grows to tens of millions of entries with per-application filtering.
Effect if it happens: Slow assessments and searches at full scale.
Mitigation: Partition the index by application. Test at projected year-three volume.

Risk: Ownership of the prototype's design and the right to reuse its ideas is unclear, or AI-generated code carries licence questions.
Effect if it happens: Delay while ownership is settled.
Mitigation: Confirm ownership and reuse rights in writing before the design phase.

Risk: The service desk cannot answer AI-specific questions such as why a control was scored a certain way.
Effect if it happens: Tickets bounce between teams. User frustration.
Mitigation: Give the service desk scripts and a clear route to the AI specialist.

Risk: Overnight batch failures go unnoticed because support is business hours only.
Effect if it happens: Assessments not ready when users expect them.
Mitigation: Make jobs restart safely. Alert at the start of the working day.

Risk: Storage and index growth after year three is not funded.
Effect if it happens: Capacity runs out.
Mitigation: Include a capacity review in the yearly service plan.

Risk: Users find the tool impractical without email notifications, evidence requests or reminders, none of which are costed.
Effect if it happens: Low day-to-day use, or late additions.
Mitigation: Test the user journey with pilot users in the design phase and confirm what is truly needed.

Risk: Recognising that the same document is used by several applications reveals to one team that another holds it.
Effect if it happens: Minor information leak.
Mitigation: Keep deduplication invisible to users.

Risk: Auditors or regulators ask for results in a standard exchange format (such as OSCAL), which is not costed.
Effect if it happens: Late addition of an export.
Mitigation: Ask internal audit which formats they need.
